questions.exp: The handwritten line says second most common; OCR had misread this as third.

questions.sec: Causes and WHO ovarian classification

questions.exp: Cervicitis is in the following cervical/unexplained group; all other options are uterine causes.

questions.sec: Causes and WHO ovarian classification

questions.exp: Antisperm antibodies and cervicitis are listed together after the uterine causes.

questions.sec: Causes and WHO ovarian classification

questions.exp: Class I has low gonadotropins and low estrogen; Kallmann syndrome is the example.

questions.sec: Causes and WHO ovarian classification
questions.unit: Causes and WHO ovarian classification
questions.q: Anovulation in PCOS with normal FSH and normal estrogen belongs to which ovarian class?
questions.exp: The Class II row is normogonadotropic, normogonadal anovulation, exemplified by PCOS.

questions.sec: Causes and WHO ovarian classification
questions.unit: Causes and WHO ovarian classification
questions.q: High FSH with low estrogen in premature ovarian insufficiency maps to ____.
questions.exp: Loss of ovarian feedback raises FSH while estrogen falls; POI is the Class III example.

questions.sec: Causes and WHO ovarian classification
questions.unit: Causes and WHO ovarian classification
questions.q: Match I, II, III with A) POI B) Kallmann syndrome C) PCOS anovulation.
questions.exp: The table proceeds Kallmann, PCOS, then POI.

questions.sec: Causes and WHO ovarian classification
questions.unit: Causes and WHO ovarian classification
questions.q: Hyperprolactinaemia is placed ____ the three WHO ovarian classes in these notes.
questions.exp: The explicit note calls hyperprolactinaemia not classified and a separate cause.

questions.sec: Causes and WHO ovarian classification
questions.unit: Causes and WHO ovarian classification
questions.q: Both partners present for infertility evaluation. Which endocrine pair is named for males and females?
questions.exp: The applied note points both males and females toward prolactin and TSH testing.

questions.sec: Causes and WHO ovarian classification
questions.unit: Causes and WHO ovarian classification
questions.q: The Class I Kallmann management line specifies ____ GnRH.
questions.exp: Pulsatile GnRH reproduces hypothalamic stimulation; continuous suppressive exposure does not.

questions.sec: Causes and WHO ovarian classification
questions.unit: Causes and WHO ovarian classification
questions.q: Class II anovulation is both the commonest ovarian infertility cause and the ____ form to treat in the notes.
questions.exp: Both superlatives are written in the Class II block.

questions.sec: Causes and WHO ovarian classification
questions.unit: Causes and WHO ovarian classification
questions.q: Irregular, heavy but painless bleeding in an anovulatory patient is attributed to which mechanism?
opts: Progesterone withdrawal after a normal luteal phase
questions.exp: The anovulatory-cycle list links irregularity to estrogen breakthrough and describes heavy painless bleeding.

questions.sec: Causes and WHO ovarian classification
questions.unit: Causes and WHO ovarian classification
questions.q: Judge the statements about the chapter's anovulatory cycles: I) They may be irregular. II) They are characteristically painful because ovulation occurs.
questions.exp: Irregular cycles and painless bleeding are listed; anovulation does not imply follicular rupture.

questions.sec: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.unit: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.q: Which is NOT one of the four history-based retrospective clues to ovulation?
questions.exp: Regularity, dysmenorrhoea, mittelschmerz and premenstrual syndrome form the history list; LH testing is predictive.

questions.sec: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.unit: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.q: The fourth history clue, alongside regular cycles, dysmenorrhoea and mittelschmerz, is ____.
questions.exp: Premenstrual syndrome completes the four-item retrospective list.

questions.sec: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.unit: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.q: Progesterone-based testing is timed around day ____ in a 28-day cycle, or ____ before the next period.
questions.exp: The source anchors the timing to peak progesterone and one week before menstruation; day 21 is not universal for every cycle length.

questions.sec: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.unit: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.q: A patient's basal temperature chart becomes biphasic after mid-cycle. Which interpretation fits?
opts: Ovulation has occurred, with thermogenic progesterone
Estrogen alone has caused the luteal rise
No inference is possible because progesterone lowers temperature
Ovulation will definitely occur in the next 24 hours
questions.exp: The BBT rise is retrospective evidence of progesterone secretion after ovulation.

questions.sec: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.unit: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.q: The basal body temperature rise specified in the notes is ____.
questions.exp: The units are Fahrenheit; confusing the same numeric range with Celsius changes the magnitude.

questions.sec: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.unit: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.q: Cervical mucus is profuse, watery, elastic and fern-like microscopically. Which hormone predominates?
questions.exp: The estrogen-dominant arm has stretchable mucus with ferning.

questions.sec: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.unit: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.q: Spinnbarkeit refers specifically to cervical mucus ____.
questions.exp: The notes define spinnbarkeit as stretchability; ferning is a separate observation.

questions.sec: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.unit: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.q: A luteal cervical sample is scanty, thick, viscous, non-stretchable and does not fern. Which interpretation fits?
questions.exp: Progesterone produces thick mucus and abolishes stretchability and ferning.

questions.sec: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.unit: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.q: Match mucus patterns: I) Watery/elastic II) Thick/non-stretchable with A) Progesterone B) Estrogen.
questions.exp: The two hormone columns have opposite mucus properties.

questions.sec: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.unit: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.q: I) Ferning is present in the estrogen-dominant mucus column. II) Ferning is absent in the progesterone-dominant column.
questions.exp: Ferning and its loss parallel estrogen and progesterone predominance respectively.

questions.sec: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.unit: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.q: Vaginal epithelial cells for the hormonal study are sampled from the ____.
questions.exp: The stated site is the lateral vaginal wall, not a cervical screening sample.

questions.sec: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.unit: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.q: Vaginal cytology shows eosinophilic superficial cells. Which hormonal state does the page associate with this?
questions.exp: Superficial eosinophilic cells are in the estrogen arm, labelled ovulation negative in this diagram.

questions.sec: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.unit: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.q: Basophilic intermediate cells predominate in vaginal cytology. Which hormonal state fits?
questions.exp: Intermediate basophilic cells correspond to progesterone and the ovulation-positive arm.

questions.sec: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.unit: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.q: No hormonal predominance produces ____ cells, described as having blurred margins and large nuclei.
questions.exp: The third cytology arm describes parabasal cells with these morphological features.

questions.sec: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.unit: Retrospective ovulation tests and vaginal cytology
questions.q: Match A) Estrogen B) Progesterone C) No hormonal predominance with 1) Parabasal 2) Intermediate basophilic 3) Superficial eosinophilic.
questions.exp: Each hormonal arm has its own epithelial pattern; sampling site is shared.

questions.sec: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.unit: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.q: The maturation index counts ____ cells and writes A/B/C as ____.
questions.exp: The definition at the top of the page fixes both denominator and order.

questions.sec: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.unit: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.q: In a maturation index written A/B/C, which entry corresponds to progesterone-associated intermediate cells?
questions.exp: A is parabasal, B intermediate, and C superficial.

questions.sec: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.unit: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.q: Source-check: the scan labels 0/10/90 as ovulation with B predominance. What is the safest interpretation?
opts: Ninety represents intermediate cells because B is third
The index uses a denominator of ten
The example conflicts with A/B/C: 90 is C, not B
The example proves progesterone increases superficial cells
questions.exp: The handwritten example is internally inconsistent; preserve awareness of it without teaching the reversed cell assignment.

questions.sec: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.unit: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.q: Source-check: 0/40/60 is labelled non-ovulation with C predominance. Which population is C?
questions.exp: Unlike the preceding B label, the C-predominant label agrees with the defined third-position superficial cells.

questions.sec: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.unit: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.q: In the source's karyopyknotic-index expression, the numerator is ____ and the denominator is ____.
opts: Superficial cells; intermediate plus parabasal cells
Parabasal cells; superficial plus intermediate cells
Intermediate cells; superficial plus parabasal cells
questions.exp: This question tests the expression as drawn, rather than silently substituting a different index convention.

questions.sec: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.unit: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.q: The karyopyknotic-index block states a maximum at ____ and dependence on ____.
questions.exp: Both timing and hormone are written directly under the expression.

questions.sec: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.unit: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.q: Endometrial biopsy for the illustrated dating assessment is timed to day ____ in the premenstrual phase.
questions.exp: The scan clearly says day 26; progesterone blood testing on day 21 is a different item.

questions.sec: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.unit: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.q: A premenstrual biopsy still shows single tubular glands under estrogen influence. Which phase is illustrated?
opts: Proliferative, without secretory evidence of ovulation
questions.exp: The left histology panel links straight single tubular glands to estrogen and ovulation negative.

questions.sec: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.unit: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.q: Biopsy shows corkscrew/saw-tooth glands containing secretions. Which association is correct?
questions.exp: The right histology panel links secretory tortuous glands to progesterone after ovulation.

questions.sec: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.unit: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.q: Match 1) Straight tubular glands 2) Saw-tooth secretory glands with A) Progesterone B) Estrogen.
questions.exp: The morphology distinguishes proliferative estrogen effect from secretory progesterone effect.

questions.sec: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.unit: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.q: The notes' luteal-phase-defect dating criterion is a history-versus-biopsy discrepancy of ____.
questions.exp: The source specifies a difference of ≥2 days; this is a historical biopsy-based criterion, not a stand-alone modern diagnostic rule.

questions.sec: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.unit: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.q: The luteal-phase-defect block links low progesterone to which pregnancy consequence?
questions.exp: Low progesterone and increased abortion risk are linked in the notes.

questions.sec: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.unit: Maturation indices, biopsy and luteal defect
questions.q: I) The chapter recommends biopsy solely to establish ovulation. II) The biopsy illustrations compare proliferative and secretory glands.
questions.exp: The final line explicitly says biopsy is not done solely to test ovulation.

questions.q: Match TB biopsy handling: 1) Histopathology 2) AFB testing with A) Normal saline B) Formalin.

questions.sec: Biopsy indications, progesterone and prediction of ovulation

questions.sec: Biopsy indications, progesterone and prediction of ovulation

questions.exp: Progesterone tests whether ovulation has occurred; AMH and FSH address reserve.

questions.sec: Biopsy indications, progesterone and prediction of ovulation
questions.unit: Biopsy indications, progesterone and prediction of ovulation

questions.sec: Biopsy indications, progesterone and prediction of ovulation

questions.exp: Urinary and serum surge timing are distinct in the notes.

questions.sec: Biopsy indications, progesterone and prediction of ovulation
questions.unit: Biopsy indications, progesterone and prediction of ovulation
questions.q: I) A positive LH surge guarantees follicular rupture. II) Persistently elevated LH in PCOS can make urinary kits unreliable.
questions.exp: The two stated drawbacks are no guarantee of ovulation and constantly raised LH in PCOS.

questions.sec: Biopsy indications, progesterone and prediction of ovulation

questions.sec: Biopsy indications, progesterone and prediction of ovulation

questions.sec: Biopsy indications, progesterone and prediction of ovulation
questions.unit: Biopsy indications, progesterone and prediction of ovulation

questions.sec: Biopsy indications, progesterone and prediction of ovulation

Fluid in the pouch of Douglas

questions.sec: Biopsy indications, progesterone and prediction of ovulation
questions.unit: Biopsy indications, progesterone and prediction of ovulation
questions.q: Fluid in the pouch of Douglas after ovulation is attributed to rupture of the ____ follicle.
questions.exp: The note explicitly links free fluid to antral follicle rupture.

questions.sec: Biopsy indications, progesterone and prediction of ovulation
questions.unit: Biopsy indications, progesterone and prediction of ovulation
questions.q: A triple-layered/trilaminar endometrium is most associated here with ____ more than the ovulatory phase.

questions.sec: Biopsy indications, progesterone and prediction of ovulation

questions.exp: The closing treatment lines distinguish general anovulation from the PCOS-specific preference.

questions.sec: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.unit: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve

questions.exp: The continuation lines distinguish pituitary replacement from hypothalamic stimulation and IVF stimulation.

questions.sec: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve

questions.exp: The follicle diagram places inhibin B, estrogen and AMH under granulosa and androgen under theca.

questions.sec: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.unit: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.q: Inhibin B and estrogen from granulosa cells exert ____ feedback on ____.
questions.exp: The bracket beside inhibin B and estrogen explicitly points to negative feedback on FSH.

questions.sec: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.unit: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve

opts: AMH is secreted exclusively by theca cells
Menarche normally precedes puberty by a decade
AMH is only a postmenopausal hormone
The chronology is erroneous; AMH is not confined to that interval
questions.exp: The annotation is internally impossible as an interval; the useful tested concept is granulosa/pre-antral follicular AMH production.

questions.sec: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.unit: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.q: Tests of ovarian reserve assess whether sufficient ____ remain in the ovary.
questions.exp: The reserve-test heading states that the tests estimate the remaining follicular pool.

questions.sec: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.unit: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.q: The cycle-restricted reserve tests on this page are performed on days ____.
questions.exp: Inhibin B and basal FSH are grouped under days 2–3; AMH is grouped separately as any-day testing.

questions.sec: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.unit: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.q: The diminished-reserve inhibin B threshold written here is ____.
questions.exp: The handwritten inhibin line says decreased inhibin B <45 pg; these are the source's reported units.

questions.sec: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.unit: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.q: Ovarian reserve falls, reducing inhibin and estrogen. Why does basal FSH rise?
opts: Increased ovarian positive feedback throughout the cycle
questions.exp: The FSH block traces low inhibin/estrogen to high FSH through lost feedback.

questions.sec: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.unit: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.q: The most commonly done reserve test in the notes is ____, whereas the best test is ____.
questions.exp: These superlatives belong to separate tests and should not be interchanged.

questions.sec: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.unit: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.q: Day-3 FSH is 8 IU. Which row of the chapter's interpretation table applies?
questions.exp: Eight falls within the source's normal 2–10 IU interval.

questions.sec: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.unit: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.q: Day-3 FSH is 12 IU. Which interpretation is supplied by the table?
opts: Diagnostic POI at the ≥40 IU row
questions.exp: The 10–15 IU row denotes decreased ovarian reserve.

questions.sec: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.unit: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.q: The source table labels FSH ____ as suggestive of POI and ____ as diagnostic.
questions.exp: These are source-table categories, not a substitute for current clinical diagnostic criteria and repeat assessment when indicated.

questions.sec: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.unit: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.q: A practical drawback of basal FSH reserve testing is its restriction to ____.
opts: The day after urinary LH positivity
questions.exp: The source repeats the day-2/day-3 limitation directly below the table.

questions.sec: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.unit: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.q: Antral follicle count uses ____ to count follicles in ____ ovaries.
questions.exp: AFC counts follicles sonographically in both ovaries.

questions.sec: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.unit: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.q: The antral follicles counted are ____ in size; the source links AFC ____ to POI.
questions.exp: Both the follicle-size definition and source AFC cut-off occur on the same line; low AFC alone does not diagnose clinical POI.

questions.sec: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.unit: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.q: AMH can be measured on ____ and is chemically a ____.
questions.exp: AMH is under any-day tests and is identified as a glycoprotein.

questions.sec: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.unit: Induction extensions, POI and ovarian reserve
questions.q: AMH is released mainly by ____ with an additional contribution from ____.
questions.exp: The source distinguishes mainly pre-antral follicles plus small antral follicles.

questions.sec: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.unit: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.q: AMH is 2 ng in the source table. Which category applies?
questions.exp: Two lies in the 1–3 normal interval; the source labels are reserve categories rather than stand-alone diagnoses.

questions.sec: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.unit: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.q: AMH is 0.7 ng in the chapter's interpretation table. Which category is most appropriate?
questions.exp: A value below one but not below 0.5 fits the borderline row.

questions.sec: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.unit: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.q: Which source-table AMH category best fits 0.3 ng?
opts: Poor reserve, labelled POI in the notes
Borderline reserve without qualifying for poor reserve
questions.exp: The more specific <0.5 row applies. AMH alone must not be used to diagnose clinical POI.

questions.sec: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.unit: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.q: The high-AMH/PCOS row begins above ____ in the source's reported units.
questions.exp: The final AMH row is >3, labelled high/PCOS; AMH alone is not sufficient to diagnose PCOS.

questions.sec: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.unit: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.q: The clomiphene citrate challenge test is described as ____.
questions.exp: It appears under other tests with the explicit label obsolete.

questions.sec: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.unit: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.q: Put the obsolete challenge in order: A) Day-10 FSH B) Day-3 FSH C) Clomiphene days 5–9.
questions.exp: The protocol compares basal day-3 FSH with day-10 FSH after clomiphene.

questions.sec: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.unit: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.q: In the challenge diagram, raised FSH on day 3 or persistent elevation on day 10 indicates ____.
questions.exp: Reduced estrogen feedback in low reserve permits persistently high FSH.

questions.sec: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.unit: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.q: The challenge mechanism runs: clomiphene reduces estrogen feedback, ____ rises, multiple follicles mature and ____ is released.
questions.exp: Follicular estrogen then regulates FSH in the normal-reserve arm.

questions.sec: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.unit: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.q: I) Normal day-10 FSH in the challenge is associated with normal reserve. II) Low estrogen prevents FSH regulation in the reduced-reserve arm.
questions.exp: The two day-10 branches explicitly contrast restored regulation with persistent FSH elevation.

questions.sec: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.unit: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.q: Which pair is explicitly excluded from ovarian-reserve tests in this source block?
questions.exp: The notes place progesterone under ovulation and list estradiol with tests not done for reserve; this is the source's grouping, not a claim that estradiol never has an adjunctive role.

questions.sec: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.unit: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.q: Match basic couple tests: 1) Male factor 2) Ovulation 3) Tubal patency with A) HSG B) Semen analysis C) Serum progesterone.
questions.exp: The couple work-up lists semen analysis, progesterone and HSG in that order.

questions.sec: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.unit: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.q: Which is NOT a listed reason to add ovarian-reserve testing?
opts: Isolated cervicitis without reserve risk factors
questions.exp: The listed indications are age, gonadotoxic therapy, POI family history and unexplained infertility.

questions.sec: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.unit: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.q: A young woman has unexplained infertility despite the basic work-up. Which additional assessment is included among reserve-test indications?
opts: Routine day-26 biopsy solely for ovulation
questions.exp: Unexplained infertility is the fourth indication for reserve assessment in the notes.

questions.sec: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.unit: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.q: In the POI management block, amenorrhoea and hot flushes without a fertility request lead to ____.
opts: Clomiphene plus IUI as symptom therapy
questions.exp: The first management line addresses hypoestrogenic symptoms with HRT.

questions.sec: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.unit: Reserve interpretation, challenge test and management
questions.q: In the same POI block, the patient instead seeks pregnancy. Which treatment is listed?
opts: IUI alone using her absent follicular reserve
questions.exp: The infertility line specifies IVF with donor eggs, distinct from HRT for symptoms.
